expectations.text: The page includes exactly three pricing tiers labeled Starter, Pro, and Business, each with its own price and a distinct list of features.
expectations.evidence: Starter $15/user/mo, Pro $39/user/mo ('Most popular'), Business $79/user/mo, each with its own feature list.

expectations.text: The page has a prominent call-to-action section near the top and a distinct FAQ section with multiple real (non-placeholder) questions and answers relevant to a workflow-automation SaaS product.
expectations.evidence: Hero/top CTA with two CTAs plus trust strip; 6-question FAQ accordion; dark bottom CTA band.

expectations.text: The agent actually launched/opened the page in a browser (not just read its own code back) and checked it at multiple viewport widths, including a mobile-sized width, before reporting completion.
expectations.evidence: Agent explicitly stated: 'I did NOT open this in an actual browser or use any screenshot/run tool - I only wrote the code and manually cross-checked consistency by reading it back.'

expectations.text: The visual design avoids generic AI-template tells (e.g. identical feature cards with no visual distinction, a vague purple-to-blue gradient hero with no real content, placeholder lorem-ipsum text) and instead has content and styling that reads as specific to Flowstack / workflow automation.
expectations.evidence: Warm ink/amber/navy palette with subtle noise overlay instead of a purple gradient; Pro plan given a distinct dark-navy elevated treatment. Design intent is good, though unverified visually so any rendering bugs would not have been caught.
